$comment: What makes a table treated: at least one analytical device that says something about its data. A node treats the table it belongs to when its role starts with one of a treatment's `rolePrefixes`, its cell's type is one of `cellTypes`, or it is a row band (`table-row-band`) of one of `rowBands` styles. Zebra banding, group rows and the implication gutter are not treatments: they keep the reader's place or structure the grid and say nothing about the data. A highlighted column or accented row is: it points the reader at the option or row the argument turns on. One definition, read by deck_gates.py (DECK_CRAFT), build-bars.mjs (BAR_TABLES_TREATED) and craft_gates.mjs (CRAFT_TABLES_PLAIN).
